clues: A dense fibrillar protein meshwork lining the nucleoplasmic surface of the inner nuclear membrane.
It is composed of type V intermediate filament proteins called lamins A, B, and C.
Hyperphosphorylation of its subunits causes disassembly of the nuclear envelope during mitotic prophase.
A small, darkly staining drumstick- or plano-convex-shaped mass of facultative heterochromatin at the nuclear periphery.
It represents a transcriptionally silenced X chromosome formed via XIST RNA coating and DNA methylation.
Normal 46,XX females have one per somatic nucleus, whereas normal 46,XY males and 45,X individuals have none.
The primary constricted region of a mitotic chromosome where two sister chromatids are most tightly joined.
Its DNA contains tandem alpha-satellite repeats and specialized CENP-A nucleosomes.
It serves as the assembly site for the kinetochore complex that attaches to spindle microtubules.
A specialized nucleoprotein cap protecting the physical ends of linear eukaryotic chromosomes.
In humans, it consists of thousands of tandem repeats of the sequence 5'-TTAGGG-3'.
Progressive shortening of this structure with each somatic cell division contributes to cellular senescence.
An organized photomicrographic display of an individual's complete set of metaphase chromosomes.
Chromosomes are arrested with colchicine, stained with Giemsa, and arranged in pairs by size and centromere position.
It is used clinically to diagnose numerical aneuploidies such as trisomy 21 and large structural translocations.
A chromosomal rearrangement occurring exclusively between two acrocentric chromosomes (13, 14, 15, 21, or 22).
Breaks near the centromeres fuse the two long arms into a single derivative chromosome while the tiny short arms are lost.
A phenotypically normal balanced carrier has 45 chromosomes and carries an elevated risk of offspring with Down or Patau syndrome.

terms.sub: Human Genome Organization and Mitochondrial DNA
clues: A phenomenon unique to extranuclear cytoplasmic genetics.
It refers to the presence of a mixture of both mutated and normal mitochondrial DNA molecules within a single cell.
Random mitotic partitioning of these organelles explains variable clinical expression among siblings with mitochondrial disorders.
A major DNA repair pathway that recognizes bulky, helix-distorting lesions such as UV-induced pyrimidine dimers.
An endonuclease complex excises a short single-stranded oligonucleotide segment containing the damaged bases.
Inherited defects in this pathway cause xeroderma pigmentosum, characterized by extreme sun sensitivity and skin cancers.
